Eat a nutrient-dense, balanced diet and practise food safety to lower infection risk. Follow your care team's nutrition advice.
Choose a balanced diet with plenty of vegetables and fruit, limit sugary and highly processed foods, and keep the skin clean.
Avoid alcohol completely, eat a balanced diet with adequate protein, and limit salt. Follow your liver specialist's advice.
Identify and avoid your personal triggers. Keep meals simple if you suspect a food reaction, and seek care for severe reactions.
Maintain a healthy weight with a diet rich in vegetables, fruit and omega-3 sources, and stay active as a clinician advises.
Eat a balanced diet rich in fruit and vegetables, maintain a healthy weight, and avoid foods you know trigger your symptoms.
Maintain a healthy weight with a balanced diet that includes calcium and vitamin D. Ask a clinician about posture and activity.
Eat soft, easy-to-digest foods and drink plenty of fluids. Keep nails short and hands clean to reduce scratching and infection.
Follow the low-fat, balanced diet your doctor advises, avoid alcohol, and take any vitamin supplements only under guidance.
Drink plenty of fluids, eat light nourishing meals such as soups, and rest well.
Drink plenty of oral fluids and eat light meals. Avoid NSAIDs unless a doctor advises, and seek urgent care for warning signs.
Follow a balanced diet low in refined sugar, with high-fibre foods and regular meal times. Work with a doctor or dietitian on a personal plan.
Eat a high-fibre diet, drink enough water, and avoid straining during bowel movements.
Do not start new medicines without advice. Keep fluids up, eat simple meals, and seek medical help for any serious reaction.
Keep skin dry, limit sugary foods and refined carbohydrates, and include whole foods as tolerated. Follow prescribed treatment.
Eat smaller meals, avoid late-night eating and common triggers such as spicy, fatty or acidic foods, and maintain a healthy weight.
Sip oral rehydration fluids, then eat bland foods such as rice, bananas and toast as tolerated. Avoid dairy and alcohol until better.
This is an emergency: call emergency services now. Long term, follow a heart-healthy diet low in salt and saturated fat, as a cardiologist advises.
Eat a balanced diet, avoid alcohol, and avoid raw or undercooked food. Follow your liver doctor's guidance.
Eat a balanced diet, avoid alcohol completely, and check with your doctor before taking any supplements or medicines.
Avoid alcohol, eat a balanced diet, and follow your liver specialist's guidance.
Stay hydrated, eat light balanced meals, avoid alcohol, and make sure food and water are safe.
Follow a low-salt diet rich in vegetables, fruit and whole grains, and limit alcohol. Discuss blood pressure targets with a doctor.
Eat a balanced diet with enough calories and calcium. Follow your endocrinologist's advice on iodine-containing foods.
Eat regular meals with complex carbohydrates and protein, and keep a fast-acting sugar source handy. Discuss repeated episodes with a doctor.
Eat a balanced diet with adequate iodine and selenium sources. Take prescribed medicine as advised, usually on an empty stomach.
Keep the affected skin clean, drink plenty of fluids, and eat a balanced diet to support healing.
Rest, drink fluids and eat light, balanced meals, and avoid alcohol. Seek medical care to find the cause.
Drink plenty of fluids and eat light meals. Antimalarial treatment must come from a doctor, so seek care promptly.
Eat regular meals, stay hydrated, and keep a diary of food triggers such as skipped meals or certain additives.
Maintain a healthy weight with a diet rich in calcium, vitamin D and omega-3 fats.
This is an emergency: seek immediate medical care. Later, follow the rehabilitation team's nutrition and swallowing advice.

Eat nourishing, protein-rich meals and drink plenty of fluids to support recovery.
Eat a balanced diet with vegetables, fruit and omega-3 sources, and limit alcohol.
Eat a protein-rich, nutritious diet and take medicines exactly as prescribed. Follow your doctor's guidance.
Drink safe, boiled or bottled water, eat freshly cooked soft foods, and avoid street food until fully recovered.
Drink plenty of water and limit caffeine and alcohol. See a doctor for diagnosis and treatment.
Keep a healthy weight, eat a high-fibre diet to prevent constipation, and limit salt.
Rest, drink fluids and eat light balanced meals. Avoid alcohol until your doctor confirms the liver has recovered.
